html:
Tashir-Dzoraget was a medieval Armenian kingdom in the north of today's Armenia, around the Lori fortress, ruled by a branch of the Bagratid royal family from 979 to 1118. It is shown here in 1100.

It was founded when King Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia gave the northern lands to one of his sons, Gurgen, who took the title of king. His line is called the Kiurikians. Its capital moved to Lori, a fortress above a river gorge. In the region stand the monasteries of Haghpat and Sanahin, founded in the 10th century by the Bagratid queen Khosrovanuysh.

The kingdom lived under pressure from the Seljuks after the fall of Ani in 1064. In 1118 David IV of the Kingdom of Georgia took Lori, and the Kiurikians moved on to small holdings to the east.
